item.title: AFP journalist wounded by Israel honored at CPJ awards
item.description:
AFP journalist Christina Assi, who lost a leg in an Israeli strike reporting from the Lebanese border and has become a vocal campaigner for reporters' safety, was honored by the Committee to Protect Journalists on Thursday.

In October 2023, Reuters journalist Issam Abdallah was killed and six others were wounded, including AFP journalists Assi and Dylan Collins, while covering the conflict near the Israeli border.

An independent AFP investigation concluded that two Israeli 120mm tank shells were fired from the Jordeikh area in northern Israel.

item.title: Somalia orders UAE ambassador to leave, citing 'invasion'
item.description:
MOGADISHU, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Somalia ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador on Thursday to leave the country within 72 hours and withdrew its own envoy from Abu Dhabi, accusing the Emirates of unspecified violations of Somalia's sovereignty that amounted to an "open invasion".

"Measures will be taken against anyone who cooperates with UAE in the invasion against Somalia," Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud said in a broadcast on the state-run news agency.

item.title: Somalia expels UAE ambassador, alleging interference
item.description:
Somalia on Thursday expelled the United Arab Emirates ambassador, accusing the Gulf nation of interfering in its internal affairs in a move blasted as "irresponsible" by Abu Dhabi.

Somalia and the UAE have quarrelled over several issues, including Abu Dhabi's perceived support for Israel's recognition of the breakaway region of Somaliland.

item.title: Gazans return after Israel army ends rare ground operation
item.description:
Weary Palestinians returned to check their belongings and assess the damage in central Gaza on Thursday, after the Israeli military said it had completed a ground operation it began the day before.

The military had launched the incursion involving tanks despite a ceasefire which came into effect in October 2025, saying it aimed to "dismantle a terror tunnel" that posed a threat to troops.

item.title: Factbox-Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group has repeatedly targeted Saudi Arabia in an intensifying campaign of drone and missile strikes on its airports, oil facilities and office buildings.

Here are some of the attacks that it has claimed to have carried out and what Saudi Arabia has said.

Houthi attacks on Saudi airports have been deadly as well as disruptive, repeatedly grounding flights in the kingdom.
